title: MCP Python SDK OAuth clients can disclose credentials to a server-selected endpoint
summary: An untrusted MCP server can redirect OAuth client credentials, authorization codes and proof material to its chosen token endpoint because issuer validation and credential binding are incomplete.

severity.rationale: Unattended OAuth clients can disclose credentials without a person approving the destination. Interactive sign-in requires user interaction.

exposure: HTTP OAuth clients holding legitimate authorization-server credentials are exposed when connecting to untrusted MCP servers. Stdio clients and MCP servers built with the SDK are not affected.

params.instructions: Check mcp version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 1.30.0 or 2.2.0 on the corresponding line. Set issuer= for ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider; migrate RFC7523OAuthClientProvider. Clear issuer-less stored registrations or bind pre-registered records to their issuer. Rotate possibly disclosed secrets and revoke tokens.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed version, explicit issuer binding and refreshed registration storage. Verify mismatched issuer metadata is rejected with a harmless fixture.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
